subject: question about syntax when having different random walks for two groups in stack

messages.author: 4a91ca21902a5bfb
messages.subject: question about syntax when having different random walks for two groups in stack
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to create a random walk for two different groups of observations in a single model. When not using a stack, this can be achieved in INLA using e.g. 
 
inla(y ~  f(time1, is1,model="rw1") + f(time2, is2,model="rw1"),
               data=testdata,
               family="gaussian",
               control.predictor=list( compute=TRUE),
               verbose=TRUE)
where is1 is a vector of 0,1 indicating group membership. Likewise for is2. When I try to apply the same approach using a stack I get an error (see my example code below, data generation is based on documentation for inla.stack()). I am hoping that somebody can point me in the right direction. 

Thanks in advance,

Jan Jaap 

n = 200
loc = matrix(runif(n*2),n,2)
mesh      = inla.mesh.create.helper(points.domain=loc, max.edge=c(0.05, 0.2))
proj.obs  = inla.mesh.projector(mesh, loc=loc)
spde = inla.spde2.matern(mesh,
                         B.tau=cbind(log(1), 1, 0),
                         B.kappa=matrix(c(log(sqrt(8)/0.2), 0, 1), 1, 3))

time1 <- time2 <-  1:n
is1 <- rep(0:1, length.out=200)
is2 <- 1-is1

field = inla.qsample(n=1, Q=inla.spde2.precision(spde, theta=c(0,0)))[,1]
y = 2*time1 + inla.mesh.project(proj.obs, field)

#########################################################
#working example without use of stack
##########################################################

testdata <- data.frame("time1"=time1, "time2"=time2, "is1"=is1, "is2"=is2)
result2 = inla(y ~  f(time1, is1,model="rw1") + f(time2, is2,model="rw1"),
               data=testdata,
               family="gaussian",
               control.predictor=list( compute=TRUE),
               verbose=TRUE)

#############################################################
#Now with stack (Fails because "variable lengths differ (found for 'is1')")
##############################################################

mystack <-  inla.stack(data    = list(y=y),
                     A       = list(1,1,1),
                     effects = list(intercept=rep(1, length(y)),
                                    time1=time1,
                                    time2=time2
                     )
)

formula = y ~ -1 + intercept + f(time1, is1, model="rw1") + f(time2, is2, model="rw1")

result2 = inla(formula,
               data=inla.stack.data(mystack),
               family="gaussian",
               control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(mystack), compute=TRUE),
               verbose=TRUE)

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] question about syntax when having different random walks for two groups in stack
parts:
Hi,

For this, I see two options to fix it:
Either add is1 and is2 to the effects lists, with list(list(intercept=…),list(time1,is1),list(time2,is2))
(I haven’t checked if the resulting NA entries in the is-vectors where time1/2 will also be NA will cause a problem or not)
Or remove the weights arguments from the f() specifications and instead use
A=list(1,Diagonal(length(is1),is1),Diagonal(length(is2),is2)),
Which has the same effect as weights in f().

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] question about syntax when having different random walks for two groups in stack
parts:
You didn’t include the actual results, but if you try the non-stack version but with an explicit intercept as a covariate (set intercept=1 in your data object) I suspect the results will be the same. The auto-intercept has a smaller precision(zero, I believe) than other fixed effects, so the models aren’t identical.
You can set the prior for a fixed effect e.g. with
  f(intercept,model=“linear”, prec.linear=…)
(Check the INLA::f documentation)

Finn

Op woensdag 8 december 2021 om 10:19:18 UTC+1 schreef finn.l...@gmail.com:

You didn’t include the actual results, but if you try the non-stack version but with an explicit intercept as a covariate (set intercept=1 in your data object) I suspect the results will be the same. The auto-intercept has a smaller precision(zero, I believe) than other fixed effects, so the models aren’t identical.
You can set the prior for a fixed effect e.g. with
  f(intercept,model=“linear”, prec.linear=…)
(Check the INLA::f documentation)

Finn

Op dinsdag 7 december 2021 om 20:14:30 UTC+1 schreef finn.l...@gmail.com:
Hi,

For this, I see two options to fix it:
Either add is1 and is2 to the effects lists, with list(list(intercept=…),list(time1,is1),list(time2,is2))
(I haven’t checked if the resulting NA entries in the is-vectors where time1/2 will also be NA will cause a problem or not)
Or remove the weights arguments from the f() specifications and instead use
A=list(1,Diagonal(length(is1),is1),Diagonal(length(is2),is2)),
Which has the same effect as weights in f().

Finn
